content: 1. Identify the cluster location and clearly define the objectives of the survey. 2. Visit each selected cluster location to establish rapport, understand potential field challenges, address questions, and resolve concerns. 3. Observe the physical layout of the location and collaborate with the gatekeeper to identify a private area suitable for conducting interviews and collecting biological specimens. 4. Discuss confidentiality protocols with key individuals in the selected clusters. 5. Set clear expectations for survey activities with the gatekeeper, including requirements for listing individuals at the cluster location, the physical space needed for interviews and specimen collection, the time required for each interview, and any testing procedures. 6. Request a comprehensive list of eligible individuals associated with the cluster location, stratified by relevant criteria (e.g., gender or age group), to facilitate sample stratification. 7. Schedule a date for participant sampling. Special Confidentiality Considerations 1. Gatekeepers do not have the right to access information collected from survey participants. 2. The list of eligible individuals should be specific enough to identify each individual uniquely within the cluster. Once all selected individuals have been approached, the list should be destroyed. 3. If a gatekeeper insists on accessing survey data, including sensitive information such as HIV test results, the cluster location should be excluded from the survey. 4. Train survey staff on participant protections and ensure they understand and sign confidentiality agreements. Survey Preparation and Implementation 1. Meet with the gatekeeper to explain the purpose of the survey and the planned activities. If a community liaison is part of the team, include them in this meeting. 2. Obtain or create a list of individuals associated with the cluster. Ensure the list includes all eligible individuals, specifies relevant stratification criteria (e.g., age), and allows for documentation of absences or unavailability on the survey day. 3. Set up a private space for conducting interviews and HIV testing, ensuring it is out of view and earshot of others. Participant Selection and Sampling 1. Randomly select individuals from the list of eligible participants using systematic or random sampling methods. Ensure all eligible individuals have an equal chance of selection. 2. If eligibility includes specific behaviors, include an eligibility screener in the survey instrument to identify individuals who may be interviewed. 3. If selected participants are unavailable, schedule alternative times for interviews and make at least three attempts to complete the survey before seeking replacements. Recruitment, Screening, and Consent 1. Approach selected individuals one-on-one to discuss the survey, its purpose, benefits, and confidentiality protections. Avoid group discussions to ensure participants feel free to decide without external pressure. 2. Escort participants to the designated interview area and assign a unique survey identification number to each participant. 3. Screen participants for eligibility using a standardized tool and document the results. If a participant is ineligible, thank them for their time. Data Collection and Testing 1. Conduct face-to-face or self-administered interviews using an electronic questionnaire. Document the mode of the interview. 2. Provide pre-test counseling, collect biological specimens, and conduct testing as per the protocol. Record all test results and provide post-test counseling. 3. Return test results if rapid testing is conducted or schedule a date to return results. Referrals and Follow-Up 1. Refer participants newly diagnosed with HIV or those not in care for HIV infection to appropriate medical care and treatment services. 2. Provide information to HIV-negative participants about future testing locations. 3. Offer referrals to other health or social services as needed. Compensation and Closeout 1. Provide compensation to participants if outlined in the protocol. 2. Conduct a debriefing session with field staff to discuss any issues or challenges encountered during data collection. Document these findings for future reference and notify the principal investigator if protocol amendments are required. Field Notes and Adjustments 1. Document any problems, barriers, or challenges encountered at the cluster location. 2. Use this information to adjust field operations for future clusters, if necessary. Time-Location Sampling (TLS) 1. Use TLS to survey populations that frequent physical venues irregularly. Create a sampling frame of all possible venue-day-time combinations to obtain a representative sample of attendees. 2. Visit selected venues during sampling events to collect data. Ensure most individuals present during the event belong to the survey’s target population. 3. TLS is particularly suitable for surveying populations such as sex workers at bars or street locations, or men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender individuals at specific venues.
